input: Look into joining a local credit union

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user may just want to research options, or they may be ready to actually apply and open an account — the depth of the plan changes entirely.
Whether this is for an individual, a couple, or a family affects what account types and membership benefits to prioritize.
Eligibility for credit unions is often tied to location, employer, or community group — knowing the user's area or affiliations determines which credit unions are even available to them.
Some credit unions require minimum deposits or fees to open accounts; knowing the user's budget shapes which options are realistic.
The user may be prioritizing a specific product (e.g., car loan, savings account, mortgage) which determines which credit union features matter most.
Understanding what problem the user is trying to solve — leaving a big bank, getting better rates, building credit — defines what 'done well' looks like.
Whether the user prefers to do everything online or needs in-person branch access affects which credit unions are practical choices.

gold.taskTitle: Research and Join a Local Credit Union
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to explore membership at a local credit union, which could involve researching options, comparing them, and completing the joining process.

questions.title: How far into this do you want to get right now?
questions.description: Is the goal to research and compare options, or to fully apply and open an account?

questions.title: What financial product are you most hoping to use?
questions.description: For example: everyday checking, a savings account, a car loan, a mortgage, or credit-building.

questions.title: What is driving you away from your current bank?
questions.description: Understanding the core problem — high fees, poor rates, bad service — defines what success looks like.

questions.title: What city or region are you located in?
questions.description: Credit union eligibility is often geographically restricted, so location determines which ones you can actually join.

questions.title: Are you opening this account just for yourself?
questions.description: Whether this is for an individual, a couple, or a family affects account types and joint membership options to consider.

questions.title: How much can you put toward an opening deposit?
questions.description: Many credit unions require a minimum share deposit; knowing your budget narrows down the realistic options.

questions.title: Do you need in-person branch access, or is online fine?
questions.description: Some credit unions are digital-first with few branches; your preference for in-person service filters the choices significantly.
